name: Melasma
description: Melasma is a common skin condition characterized by dark, irregularly shaped patches on the face. It usually affects women more than men and can be triggered by hormonal changes or exposure to sunlight.
causes: Hormonal Changes (e.g., pregnancy, birth control pills)
symptoms: Dark, brownish-gray patches on the face, particularly the cheeks, forehead, bridge of the nose, and chin
May worsen during summer months or with increased sun exposure
risk_factors: Females who use hormonal birth control
People with a family history of melasma
Those with skin of color (African American, Hispanic, Asian)
Individuals with a higher Fitzpatrick skin type (III-VI)
ingredients_to_avoid: Irritating Ingredients (e.g., Salicylic Acid, Retinoids without professional guidance)

daily_routine.purpose: Remove dirt and impurities from the skin.
Balance the skin's pH and prepare it for further products.
Helps to even out skin tone and reduce dark patches.
Protect the skin from UV damage which can worsen melasma. Use broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher every day.

natural_remedies: Use Cucumber Slices for Cooling and Soothing
Consume Foods High in Antioxidants (e.g., berries, nuts)
lifestyle_tips: Wear Broad-Brimmed Hats to Protect from Sun
Seek Shade During Peak Sunlight Hours
Use Mineral Sunscreens with Zinc or Titanium Dioxide
common_myths: Melasma can be completely cured in one treatment.
The condition is purely cosmetic and does not require medical attention.
when_to_consult_doctor: If self-care measures do not improve the condition, if there are sudden changes or new onset of patches, or if you have concerns about your symptoms.

severity_levels.mild: Visible dark patches that are not extensive. No significant impact on self-esteem or daily activities.
severity_levels.moderate: Visible patches that cover a larger area of the face, causing mild discomfort or concern about appearance.
severity_levels.severe: Widespread dark patches that significantly affect self-confidence and quality of life.

expert_tips: Consistency is key in treating melasma. Stick to your skincare routine even when you do not see immediate results.
Combining treatments can be more effective than using a single product or therapy alone.
